answers.answer: The top region card is revealed and the King is placed there. Each player receives a region card and places their Grande in that home region. Of each player's initial ten Caballeros, 2 go to the home region, 1 to scoring track space 1, and 7 to their court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal top region card and place the King there; deal one card to each player for their Grande/home region; each player places 2 Caballeros in home, 1 on scoring track space 1, and 7 in their court.

answers.answer: The youngest player begins in round 1. In later rounds, the player who played lowest last round begins. Other players' seating direction is not specified. Values must be different, so a played value may not be matched.
answers.evidence: Power cards: “Starting with the leader (youngest in round 1, then whoever played lowest last round)” and “All played values must be different.”

answers.answer: Players take turns from highest to lowest power-card value. On their turn, each adds from the provinces to their court the number of Caballeros shown on their power card. Recruitment happens before discarding that card and selecting an action card.
answers.evidence: Player turns (highest to lowest power card): first “Adds Caballeros from the provinces to their court (number shown on power card),” then discards the card and selects an action card.

answers.answer: If the provinces run out, a player may remove their own Caballeros from the board to their court. The summary does not say which board locations are protected from supplying those Caballeros.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “If provinces run out, a player may remove their own Caballeros from the board to their court.”

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment may go to regions adjacent to the King's region or into the Castillo, and it may be split among multiple adjacent regions and the Castillo. The card shows the maximum. The summary does not explicitly say whether using fewer than the full allowance is permitted.
answers.evidence: Deploying Caballeros: “regions adjacent to the King or into the Castillo”; “Maximum number shown”; “Can split between multiple adjacent regions and the Castillo.”

answers.answer: Deployment and the special action may be done in either order, and the special action is optional. Whether the two activities may be interleaved is not specified.
answers.evidence: Turn structure: perform the two activities “(in either order)” and the “Special action” is “(optional).”

answers.answer: After a turn, the chosen action card is turned over. The summary does not state what happens to unselected face-up cards at the end of a round. The King card is turned face up every round and never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn structure: “Turns over the chosen action card.” Special Rules: “The King card (5-pile) is turned face up every round and never permanently discarded.”

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or scoreboard may be moved into or out of the King's region. The region may still be scored; the summary gives a King's bonus when it is scored. Moving the King is listed as a special action, which would change which region is the King's region, but the summary does not explicitly describe that effect on the restriction.
answers.evidence: The King's Region: “No Caballeros, Grandes, or scoreboards may be moved into or out of the King's Region. No exceptions”; King's Bonus applies “when it is scored.” Special actions include “move the King.”

answers.answer: Players announce how many Caballeros they add to the Castillo. The King’s location does not restrict entry: Caballeros can always enter the Castillo. They leave during general scoring, when the Castillo is emptied and they are moved to chosen regions. If the Castillo is scored via an action card, it is not emptied.
answers.evidence: The Castillo: Caballeros are placed secretly and “players announce how many they add”; “During general scoring only: Castillo is scored, then emptied”; deployment says Caballeros “can always enter the Castillo regardless of King's position.”

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. First, each player secretly selects a destination region on their secrecy disk; next the Castillo is scored; then its Caballeros are redistributed to the selected regions; finally, the regions are scored in round-chart order. Thus destinations are chosen before the Castillo is scored/revealed.
answers.evidence: General Scoring: “Each player secretly selects a region ... for Castillo redistribution”; then “Score the Castillo”; then “Move Castillo Caballeros”; then “Score each region.”

answers.answer: A player's Castillo Caballeros all go to one region, so they cannot be split, and the chosen destination cannot be the King's region. Keeping them in the Castillo is not listed as an option. The summary does not say what happens if a player selects the King's region despite the prohibition.
answers.evidence: General Scoring: “all of one player's must go to a single region, cannot be the King's Region.”

answers.answer: The three players tied at four Caballeros each receive the lower tied position's points, which is the second-place value of 3; the higher position is eliminated. The summary does not specify what the player with three Caballeros scores after this three-way tie. Grandes do not count as Caballeros in the standard game.
answers.evidence: Region Scoring: “Tied players each receive the points for the lower position and the higher position is eliminated.” Special Rules: a Grande “does not count as a Caballero” in the standard game.

answers.answer: The player with 4 scores 6 points; the player with 3 scores 4; and each of the two players tied at 2 receives the lower tied position's 2 points, with the higher position eliminated.
answers.evidence: Region Scoring defines first/second/third as the three scoreboard values and says tied players each receive the points for the lower position while the higher position is eliminated.

answers.answer: The summary does not specify which scoreboard ranks pay in two-player or three-player games, or the outcome of a two-player tie for first.
answers.evidence: The summary says regions show three scoring values for most, second, and third, but does not describe player-count-specific scoreboards or a two-player tie rule.

answers.answer: The King's Bonus is 2 points when the King's region is scored, for the player with a sole Caballero majority there; it is not awarded on a tie for first. The Home Bonus is 2 points when a region is scored, for its sole Caballero-majority holder if their Grande is there; it is not awarded on a tied majority.
answers.evidence: King's Bonus: “+2 points when it is scored” and “Not awarded if tied for first.” Home Bonus: “+2 points if their Grande is in that region” and “No Home Bonus ... for a tied majority.”

answers.answer: Specially scoring the Castillo does not empty it or redistribute its Caballeros. It is scored via the action card, and the Caballeros remain there; emptying occurs only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: The Castillo section says it is emptied “During general scoring only” and, “If scored via action cards, it is NOT emptied.”

answers.answer: The summary says scoreboards may not be moved into or out of the King's region. It does not specify whether a mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo, stacked on another scoreboard, or rotated to change its values.
answers.evidence: The King's Region restriction includes “scoreboards”; no Castillo placement, stacking, or rotation rule for scoreboards is given.

answers.answer: The summary says certain action cards can move a Grande, subject to the King's Region restriction. It does not state legal source/destination rules beyond that restriction, whether another Grande may already be at the destination, or what changes after the move.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “Certain action cards can move it, subject to the King’s Region restriction.”

answers.answer: The summary only says power cards can be recovered via certain action cards. It does not identify which card may be returned, whether the current turn's card is eligible, or whether the choice must be revealed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “Power cards are permanently discarded after use (can only be recovered via certain action cards).” No further recovery procedure is included.

answers.answer: The standard game ends after 9 rounds. The player with the most points wins.
answers.evidence: Game End: “After 9 rounds ... Player with the most points wins.”
